purpose: Browser/device notification control center: background push, in-tab delivery, tab indicators, device filtering, data usage and sound preferences.
primaryGoal: Understand notification availability and configure this browser without confusing device rules with server-wide routing or quiet hours.

dataSources.behavior: Public key 404 maps to unconfigured/null; query keys, cancellation, retry:false for public key, stale times and mutation invalidation/toasts are existing contracts. Browser permission, service-worker registration and PushManager subscription are separate local sources.

Local key teslasync-web-push-prefs stores alert/export booleans. SSE alert/export_status listeners deliver hidden-tab OS notifications; alert sound listener is independent of visibility and permission. Quiet-suppressed/test alerts are excluded. SSE transport internals and server payload correctness were not exercised.

Shared settings query feeds tab KPI and independent panel. Missing tab booleans default on; saves preserve the full cached settings object. useDataState retains usable data and exposes refresh/fatal distinction.

Vehicle list is for an independent notification-delivery policy, not a duplicate workspace selector. Device policy is persisted under teslasync:device-notification-prefs:v1, sanitized, mirrored across tabs and posted to the existing service worker. Policy implementation was not independently validated.
Local external store and cross-tab storage synchronization; master, seven category toggles and normalized volume. Testing intentionally overrides master/category and raises zero volume to 0.5.
Existing auto/on/off device control and source/effect explanations. Hook and service-worker enforcement internals were not inspected.

duplicatedPatterns.detail: The mounted shell already invokes useNotificationListener at Layout.tsx:850. This page invokes it again, registering another alert sound callback (hook lines 192-210) and hidden-tab notification callbacks. Preferences are separate useState snapshots, so same-tab page toggles do not update the shell's closure. Duplicate sounds and contradictory delivery preferences are source-backed risks, not runtime-observed outcomes.
duplicatedPatterns.fix: Keep one shell-owned delivery listener; expose the same persisted preference source to page controls through an existing context/external-store pattern without mounting another delivery listener. Preserve alert/export drillthrough and exclusions.

duplicatedPatterns.detail: Even when supplied the page's webPush object, the card unconditionally mounts another useWebPush. The listener and device panel also mount independent instances. Cached queries can deduplicate requests, but permission/subscription useState is not shared.
duplicatedPatterns.fix: Reuse an existing centralized permission/subscription source; do not call hooks conditionally. A hook-owning wrapper can preserve standalone-card use while a presentation-only child accepts the already-owned source.

observedSource: Page sections have localized aria-labels; decorative feature icons commonly use aria-hidden.
Permission and push status include words, not only color.
Device test result uses role=status and aria-live=polite; tab saving state uses aria-busy and polite feedback.
Sound test buttons have category-specific accessible names.
Push key checking, error/retry, unsupported/unconfigured, denied, subscribed and action failure have explicit UI.
Subscriptions have skeleton/fatal error/stale refresh feedback and retained rows.
Tab settings have independent skeleton/error/empty/retry and saving guards; retained data is not replaced on refresh failure.
Vehicle policy selection retains unavailable saved IDs and distinguishes loading/error/empty.
Sound preferences and device preferences are local and remain available without a page-wide network gate.

issues.detail: Permission is initialized separately in every hook instance and only updated by that instance's requestPermission (lines 78-82). The page's granted UI can therefore diverge from useNotificationListener's separate permission snapshot (listener lines 98,112), or the device test panel's snapshot (panel line 107), after an enable action. Browser site-settings changes also have no synchronization here.
issues.fix: Share observed permission across existing consumers and refresh browser truth at appropriate lifecycle points; retain explicit unsupported/denied/default meanings and user-gesture-only permission prompts.

issues.rule: MDC-026 unknown is not a negative measurement
issues.detail: Subscription begins false while getSubscription is unresolved. Lookup failures at lines 68-72 are swallowed. BrowserPushChannelCard.tsx:82-85 only defers availability for the public-key query, so it can show 'Not subscribed' when device subscription truth is checking or unavailable.
issues.fix: Expose existing subscription lookup as checking/known/unavailable with retry and only show definitive subscribed/not-subscribed labels after successful device lookup.

issues.detail: Server unsubscribe errors are caught and ignored; browser unsubscribe errors are also ignored (lines 217-224), and the function returns true at line 225. The boolean returned by PushSubscription.unsubscribe is not checked. The card's actionFailed state only catches false/rejection, so it may clear the device to not-subscribed without confirming either removal.
issues.fix: Preserve the deliberate best-effort browser cleanup, but expose separate server/browser outcomes and re-read subscription truth. Report partial failure and retry rather than treating user intent as confirmed success.

issues.rule: MDC-026 / mission section 23 explicit empty state
issues.detail: Successful zero-row subscription data hides the registered-device subsection entirely. There is no explicit empty-list explanation to distinguish an empty server registry from the adjacent device-local subscription verdict.
issues.fix: Retain the registered-device heading and add a localized settled-empty explanation using the existing EmptyState; keep source loading/error and retained-data behavior independent.

visualIssues.detail: The shared low-bandwidth status paragraph uses raw text-xs rather than the existing role renderer, while its neighboring caption/help already use shared typography.
visualIssues.fix: Use Text as=p with the equivalent caption/body role and preserve data-testid, data-enabled, data-source and full explanatory text.

architectureIssues.detail: Sound category labels use a computed translation key. The neighboring device policy component explicitly uses a static key map because the repository extractor cannot see computed keys (DeviceNotificationPrefsPanel.tsx:72-76). Catalog coverage and extraction failure were not executed or independently verified.
architectureIssues.fix: Use a typed static category-to-key map with the existing seven fallbacks; retain all category identities and canonical catalogs.

dataBehavior: Preserve explicit distinction among background push, hidden-tab Notification API delivery, device-side policy and server-wide settings.
Device test is not an end-to-end server push test; preserve its policy evaluation and browser-only success/suppression/error messages.
Preserve all stored keys/defaults, settings full-object writes, query keys, cancellation, invalidation/broadcast, stale times and retry semantics.
No physical measurement conversion exists in this orchestration; booleans, counts, severity, IDs, local quiet times and normalized audio volume must not be treated as SI measurements.
Do not add a workspace date selector: this is a device settings route, absent from RANGE_ENABLED_PATHS.
Notifications are in VEHICLE_DISABLED_PREFIXES; preserve local notification-policy vehicle selection, which is not a duplicate global workspace selector.
Preserve server cost/silent-push caveat, iOS Home Screen requirements, browser-blocked guidance and low-bandwidth effect explanations.
Keep every independent section visible during unrelated source failure; preserve retained usable settings/device rows and saved unavailable vehicle IDs.
preservation.palette: Current feature source uses restrained cyan-300/emerald/rose/amber accents and semantic UI variants, not direct neon text/glow. neonColorMap is used only for its text entry, which currently maps to subdued colors (tokens.ts:21-22); its name alone is not a violation. Prefer semantic tokens for any future accent changes; composed contrast remains unverified.
